questions.q: Time taken by light to travel in two different materials $A$ and $B$ of refractive indices ${\mu}_{A}$ and ${\mu}_{B}$ of same thickness is ${t}_{1}$ and ${t}_{2}$ respectively. If ${t}_{2} - {t}_{1} = 5 \times {10}^{- 10}s$ and the ratio of ${\mu}_{A}$ to ${\mu}_{B}$ is $1: 2$. Then the thickness of material, in meter is: (Given ${v}_{A}$ and ${v}_{B}$ are velocities of light in $A$ and $B$ materials respectively).
questions.solution:
The speed of light in a medium is inversely proportional to the refractive index of the material. Therefore,

$\dfrac{{\mu}_{A}}{{\mu}_{B}} = \dfrac{{v}_{B}}{{v}_{A}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Let the thickness is $d$

$⇒ {t}_{2} - {t}_{1} = \dfrac{d}{{v}_{B}} - \dfrac{d}{{v}_{A}} = 5 \times {10}^{- 10}s$

As ${v}_{A} = 2{v}_{B} ⇒ d = 5 \times {10}^{- 10} \times 2{v}_{B}$

$⇒ d = 5 \times {10}^{- 10} \times {v}_{A}m$.

questions.q: A parallel beam of light is allowed to fall on a transparent spherical globe of diameter $30cm$ and refractive index $1 . 5$. The distance from the centre of the globe at which beam of light can converge is _____ $mm$.
questions.solution:
For the refraction at the left surface, $u = - \infty , R = + 15cm$.

$\dfrac{{\mu}_{2}}{v} - \dfrac{{\mu}_{1}}{u} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{2} - {\mu}_{1}}{R}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1 . 5}{{v}_{1}} - \dfrac{1}{- \infty} = \dfrac{1 . 5 - 1}{+ 15}$

$⇒ {v}_{1} = 45cm$

For the refraction at the right surface, $u = 45 - 30 = 15cm, R = - 15cm$

$\dfrac{{\mu}_{2}}{v} - \dfrac{{\mu}_{1}}{u} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{2} - {\mu}_{1}}{R}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{{v}_{2}} - \dfrac{1 . 5}{15} = \dfrac{1 - 1 . 5}{- 15}$

$⇒ {v}_{2} = 7 . 5cm$

Therefore, the distance from the centre where the beam will converge is,

$15 + 7 . 5 = 22 . 5cm = 225mm$

questions.q: The refracting angle of a prism is $A$ and refractive index of the material of the prism is $cot\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)$. Then the angle of minimum deviation will be
questions.solution:
As we know, angle of minimum deviation is given by, $⇒ \mu = \dfrac{sin\dfrac{\left({\delta}_{m} + A\right)}{2}}{sin\dfrac{A}{2}}$

$⇒ cot\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right) = \dfrac{sin\dfrac{\left({\delta}_{m} + A\right)}{2}}{sin\dfrac{A}{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{cos\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)}{sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{sin\dfrac{\left({\delta}_{m} + A\right)}{2}}{sin\dfrac{A}{2}}$

$⇒ sin\left(90 ° - \dfrac{A}{2}\right) = sin\left(\dfrac{{\delta}_{m} + A}{2}\right)$

Therefore, $90 ° - \dfrac{A}{2} = \dfrac{{\delta}_{m} + A}{2}$⇒ {\delta}_{m} = 180 ° - 2A$

questions.solution:

questions.q: A light ray is incident, at an incident angle ${\theta}_{1}$, on the system of two plane mirrors ${M}_{1}$ and ${M}_{2}$ having an inclination angle $75 °$ between them (as shown in figure). After reflecting from mirror ${M}_{1}$ it gets reflected back by the mirror ${M}_{2}$ with an angle of reflection $30 °$. The total deviation of the ray will be _____ degree.
questions.solution:
From the above figure, ${i}_{2} = 30 °$,

Now,

$∠ OBA + ∠ ABR + ∠ RBP = 180 ° ⇒ 2 ∠ OBA + 60 ° = 180 ° ⇒ ∠ OBA = 60 °$

In triangle $OAB$,

$∠ OBA + ∠ AOB + ∠ OAB = 180 ° ⇒ 60 ° + 75 ° + ∠ OAB = 180 ° ⇒ ∠ OAB = 45 °$

And,

$∠ OAB + ∠ BAI + ∠ IAQ = 180 ° ⇒ 2 ∠ OAB + 2{i}_{1} = 180 ° ⇒ {i}_{1} = 45 °$

Now the total deviation of the ray will be,

$\delta = 360 ° - 2\left({i}_{1} + {i}_{2}\right) ⇒ \delta = 360 ° - 2\left(30 ° + 45 °\right)\delta = 210 °$

questions.q:
A light wave travelling linearly in a medium of dielectric constant $4$, incidents on the horizontal interface separating medium with air. The angle of incidence for which the total intensity of incident wave will be reflected back into the same medium will be :
(Given : relative permeability of medium ${\mu}_{r} = 1$)
questions.solution:
Relative refractive index is $\mu = \sqrt{{\mu}_{r}{ε}_{r}} = \sqrt{4 \times 1} = 2$

Now, for complete reflection, $\theta > {\theta}_{c}$, where, ${\theta}_{c}$ is critical angle.

Now, critical angle is $sin{\theta}_{c} = \dfrac{1}{\mu} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ {\theta}_{c} = \sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) ⇒ {\theta}_{c} = 30 °$

So, the angle of incidence for which the total intensity of incident wave will be reflected back into the same medium is $\theta > 30 °$ i.e., $60 °$.

questions.q: The difference of speed of light in the two media $A$ and $B\left({v}_{A} - {v}_{B}\right)$ is $2 . 6 \times {10}^{7}m{s}^{- 1}$. If the refractive index of medium $B$ is $1 . 47$, then the ratio of refractive index of medium $B$ to medium $A$ is: (Given : speed of light in vacuum $c = 3 \times {10}^{8}{ms}^{- 1}$)
questions.solution:
The speed of light in the medium $B$ will be, ${v}_{B} = \dfrac{c}{{\mu}_{B}}$

The speed of light in the medium $A$ will be, ${v}_{A} = \dfrac{c}{{\mu}_{A}}$.

Now,

${v}_{A} - {v}_{B} = c\left(\dfrac{1}{{\mu}_{A}} - \dfrac{1}{{\mu}_{B}}\right) ⇒ 2 . 6 \times {10}^{7} = 3 \times {10}^{8} \times \left(\dfrac{1}{{\mu}_{A}} - \dfrac{1}{1 . 47}\right) ⇒ {\mu}_{A} = 1 . 13$

questions.q: Two identical thin biconvex lenses of focal length $15cm$ and refractive index $1 . 5$ are in contact with each other. The space between the lenses is filled with a liquid of refractive index $1 . 25$. The focal length of the combination is _____ $cm .$
questions.solution:
For convex lenses, let radius of curvature is $R$. Then,

$\dfrac{1}{15cm} = \left(1 . 5 - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{- R}\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{R} = \dfrac{1}{15} ⇒ R = 15cm$

Now for concave lens,

$\dfrac{1}{{f}_{concave}} = \left(1 . 25 - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{- R} - \dfrac{1}{R}\right)$

$= \dfrac{1}{4} \times - \dfrac{2}{R} = \dfrac{- 1}{30}$

$\dfrac{1}{{f}_{eff}} = \dfrac{1}{15} + \dfrac{1}{15} - \dfrac{1}{30} = - \dfrac{1}{10}$

$⇒ {f}_{eff} = - 10cm$

Object distance, $u = - 1.9m = 190cm$

Magnitude of velocity $= 0 . 1m{s}^{- 1}$

questions.q:
Three rays of light, namely red $\left(R\right)$, green $( G )$ and blue $( B )$ are incident on the face $PQ$ of a right angled prism $PQR$ as shown in figure.

The refractive indices of the material of the prism for red, green and blue wavelength are $1 . 27, 1 . 42 and 1 . 49$ respectively. The colour of the ray(s) emerging out of the face $PR$ is :
questions.solution:
Assuming that the right angled prism is an isoceles prism, so the other angles will be $45 °$ each.

$⇒$ Each incident ray will make an angle of $45 °$ with the normal at face $PR$.

$⇒$ The wavelength corresponding to which the incidence angle is less than the critical angle, will pass through $PR$.

$⇒ {\theta}_{C} =$ critical angle

$⇒ {\theta}_{C} = \sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\mu}\right)$

$⇒$ If ${\theta}_{C} \ge 45 °$

the light ray will pass

$⇒ {\left({\theta}_{C}\right)}_{Red} = \sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{1 . 27}\right) = 51 . 94 °$

Red will pass.

$⇒ {\left({\theta}_{C}\right)}_{Green} = \sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{1 . 42}\right) = 44 . 76 °$

Green will not pass

$⇒ {\left({\theta}_{C}\right)}_{Blue} = \sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{1 . 49}\right) = 42 . 15 °$

Blue will not pass

$⇒$ So only red will pass through $PR$.

questions.q: The thickness at the centre of a plano convex lens is $3mm$ and the diameter is $6cm .$ If the speed of light in the material of the lens is $2 \times {10}^{8}{ms}^{- 1} .$ The focal length of the lens is ___________.
questions.solution:
${R}^{2} = {r}^{2} + ( R - t{)}^{2}$

${R}^{2} = {r}^{2} + {R}^{2} + {t}^{2} - 2Rt$

Neglecting ${t}^{2},$ we get

$R = \dfrac{{r}^{2}}{2t}$

$∴ \dfrac{1}{f} = \left(\mu - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{\infty}\right) = \dfrac{\mu - 1}{R}$

$f = \dfrac{R}{\mu - 1} = \dfrac{{r}^{2}}{2t ( \mu - 1 )} = \dfrac{{\left(3 \times {10}^{- 2}\right)}^{2}}{2 \times 3 \times {10}^{- 3} \times \left(\dfrac{3}{2} - 1\right)}$

$= \dfrac{9 \times {10}^{- 4}}{6 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 1} \times 2$

$f = 0 . 3m = 30cm$

questions.q: For a concave lens of focal length $f$, the relation between object and image distance $u$ and $v,$ respectively, from its pole can best be represented by ($u = v$ is the reference line):
questions.solution:
From the lens formula, $\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$

$⇒ v = f - \dfrac{{f}^{2}}{u + f}$

now, if we plot a graph between $u\text{and}v$

When $u \to \infty ; v = f - \dfrac{{f}^{2}}{\infty} = f$

and for $u \to 0; v = 0$

Given that $u = v$is a reference line, therefore, $\dfrac{d v}{d u} = 0 + \dfrac{{f}^{2}}{{\left(u + f\right)}^{2}}$

${\dfrac{d v}{d u}}_{u = 0} = 0 + \dfrac{{f}^{2}}{{\left(0 + f\right)}^{2}} = 1$

The equation of tangent of the curve at the origin, $v - 0 = 1\left(u - 0\right) ⇒ v = u$

questions.q: Two light waves having the same wavelength $\lambda$ in vacuum are in phase initially. Then the first wave travels a path ${L}_{1}$ through a medium of refractive index ${n}_{1}$while the second wave travels a path of length ${L}_{2}$ through a medium of refractive index ${n}_{2}$. After this the phase difference between the two waves is:
questions.solution:
The optical path between any two points is proportional to the time of travel.

The distance traversed by light in a medium of refractive index $\mu$ in time $t$ is given by $d = vt$ .......(i)

Where $v$ is velocity of light in the medium. The distance traversed by light in a vacuum in this time,

$s = ct$

$= c \times \dfrac{d}{v}$ [from equation (i)]

$= d\dfrac{c}{v} = \mu d$ .....(ii) (Since$\mu = \dfrac{c}{v}$)

This distance is the equivalent distance in vacuum and is called optical path.

Here, optical path for first ray $= {n}_{1}{L}_{1}$

Optical path for second ray $= {n}_{2}{L}_{2}$

Path difference $= {n}_{1}{L}_{1} - {n}_{2}{L}_{2}$

Now, phase difference $= \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda} \times$path difference

$= \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda} \times \left({n}_{1}{L}_{1} - {n}_{2}{L}_{2}\right)$

After this the phase difference between the two waves is:
questions.explanation:
The optical path between any two points is proportional to the time of travel.

The distance traversed by light in a medium of refractive index $\mu$ in time $t$ is given by $d = vt$ .......(i)

Where $v$ is velocity of light in the medium. The distance traversed by light in a vacuum in this time,

$s = ct$

$= c \times \dfrac{d}{v}$ [from equation (i)]

$= d\dfrac{c}{v} = \mu d$ .....(ii) (Since$\mu = \dfrac{c}{v}$)

This distance is the equivalent distance in vacuum and is called optical path.

Here, optical path for first ray $= {n}_{1}{L}_{1}$

Optical path for second ray $= {n}_{2}{L}_{2}$

Path difference $= {n}_{1}{L}_{1} - {n}_{2}{L}_{2}$

Now, phase difference $= \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda} \times$path difference

$= \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda} \times \left({n}_{1}{L}_{1} - {n}_{2}{L}_{2}\right)$

questions.q: A concave mirror has radius of curvature of $40cm .$ It is at the bottom of a glass that has water filled up to $5cm$ (see figure). If a small particle is floating on the surface of water, its image as seen, from directly above the glass, is at a distance $d$ from the surface of water. The value of $d$ is close to: (Refractive index of water $= 1.33 )$
questions.solution:
Given
$u = - 5cm$
$f = \dfrac{- R}{2} = - \dfrac{40}{2} = - 20cm$
Now
$\dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$
$\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{- 20} = \dfrac{1}{\left(- 5\right)}$
$∴ \text{v} = + \dfrac{20}{3}cm$
Then
Object distance $d = 5 + \dfrac{20}{3} = \dfrac{35}{3}cm$ (below water surface)
The image after refraction
$d' = d\left(\dfrac{{\mu}_{2}}{{\mu}_{1}}\right)$
$= \dfrac{35}{3}\left(\dfrac{1}{1.33}\right)$
$= 8.77$
${d}^{'} ≃ 8.8cm$

questions.q: One plano-convex and one plano-concave lens of the same radius of curvature $R$ but of different materials are joined side by side as shown in the figure. If the refractive index of the material of $1$ is ${\mu}_{1}$ and that of $2$ is${\mu}_{2}$, then the focal length of the combination is:
questions.solution:
From lens maker’s formula,
$\dfrac{1}{f} = \left(\mu - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{{R}_{1}} - \dfrac{1}{{R}_{2}}\right)$
$\dfrac{1}{{f}_{1}} = \left({\mu}_{1} - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{\infty} - \dfrac{1}{\left(- R\right)}\right) = \dfrac{{\mu}_{1} - 1}{R}$
$\dfrac{1}{{f}_{2}} = \left({\mu}_{2} - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{\left(- R\right)} - \dfrac{1}{\infty}\right) = - \dfrac{\left({\mu}_{2} - 1\right)}{R}$
$\dfrac{1}{{f}_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{{f}_{1}} + \dfrac{1}{{f}_{2}} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{1} - 1}{R} - \dfrac{{\mu}_{2} - 1}{R}$
$= \dfrac{{\mu}_{1} - {\mu}_{2}}{R}$
${f}_{eq} = \dfrac{R}{{\mu}_{1} - {\mu}_{2}}$

questions.q: A convex lens (of focal length $20cm$ ) and a concave mirror, having their principal axes along the same lines, are kept $80cm$ apart from each other. The concave mirror is to the right of the convex lens. When an object is kept at a distance of $30cm$ to the left of the convex lens, its image remains at the same position even if the concave mirror is removed. The maximum distance of the object for which this concave mirror, by itself would produce a virtual image would be:
questions.solution:
Image formed by lens
$\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$
$⇒ \dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{1}{20}$
$⇒ \dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1}{30}$
$⇒ v = 60cm$
In the image remains at the same position even if the concave mirror is removed indicates that the image formed by lens is formed at the center of curvature of spherical mirror.
$∴$ Radius of curvature of mirror $= 80 - 60 = 20cm$
Focal length, $f = 10cm$
For virtual image to be formed, object is to be kept between focus and pole. Hence, the maximum distance of object from spherical mirror for which virtual image is formed will be its focal length 10cm

questions.q:
In figure, the optical fiber is $l = 2m$ long and has a diameter of $d = 20\mum .$ If a ray of light is incident on one end of the fiber at angle ${\theta}_{1} = 40 °$ , the number of reflections it makes before emerging from the other end is close to:
(refractive index of fiber is $1.31$ , $sin40 ° = 0.64$ and $\sin^{- 1} ⁡ 0.49 = 30 °$ .)
questions.solution:
Let ${n}_{1}$ and ${n}_{2}$ be the refractive indices of the air and optical fibre respectively. Applying Snell's law at Q, we get:

${n}_{1}sin{\theta}_{1} = {n}_{2}sin{\theta}_{2}$

$sin{40}^{∘} = 1 . 31 \times sin{\theta}_{2}$

$⇒ sin{\theta}_{2} = \dfrac{0 . 64}{1 . 31} = 0 . 4885 \approx 0 . 5$

$⇒ {\theta}_{2} = {30}^{∘}$

The distance covered along the length of the optical fibre after one reflection:

$QN = RN{cot \theta}_{2}$

$= 20 \times {10}^{- 6} \times cot{30}^{∘} = 20\sqrt{3} \times {10}^{- 6}m$

The reflections take place throughout the length of the optical fibre.

Length of the wire$= 2m$

Total number of reflections along its length$= \dfrac{Lengthofthewire}{distancecoveredinonereflectionalongthelength}$

$= \dfrac{2 \times {10}^{6}}{20\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{100000}{\sqrt{3}} = 57735 . 02 \approx 57000$

questions.q: An upright object is placed at a distance of $40cm$ in front of a convergent lens of focal length $20cm .$ A convergent mirror of focal length $10cm$ is placed at a distance of $60cm$ on the other side of the lens. The position and size of the final image will be:
options: $40cm$ from the convergent lens, twice the size of the object
$20cm$ from the convergent mirror, twice the size of the object
$40cm$ from the convergent lens, same size of the object
$20cm$ from the convergent mirror, same size of the object
questions.solution:
First refraction, $u = - 40cm; f = + 20cm$
From lens formula, $\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$
$\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{- 40} = \dfrac{1}{20} ⇒ \dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1}{40}$
$v = + 40cm$
${m}_{1} = - 1$
First reflection, $u = - 20cm; f = - 10cm$
From mirror formula, $\dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$
$\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{20} = \dfrac{1}{- 10}$
$\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{- 10} + \dfrac{1}{20} ⇒ v = - 20cm$
${m}_{2} = - 1$
Second refraction, $u = - 40cm, f = + 20cm$
From lens formula, $\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{- 40} = \dfrac{1}{20} ⇒ v = + 40cm$
${m}_{3} = - 1$
${m}_{total} = {m}_{1} \times {m}_{2} \times {m}_{3} = - 1$
Finally, image will be at distance $40cm$ from lens and is of same size as object.

questions.q: A plano - convex lens (focal length ${f}_{2}$ , refractive index ${\mu}_{2},$ radius of curvature R) fits exactly into a plano - concave lens (focal length ${f}_{1},$ refractive index ${\mu}_{1},$ radius of curvature R). Their plane surfaces are parallel to each other. Then, the focal length of the combination will be:
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{1}{{f}_{1}} = \left({\mu}_{1} - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{- R} - \dfrac{1}{\omega}\right)\dfrac{1}{{f}_{2}} = \left({\mu}_{2} - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{\omega}\right)$

When joined together

$\dfrac{1}{{f}_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{{f}_{1}} + \dfrac{1}{{f}_{2}} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{2} - 1}{- R} + \dfrac{{\mu}_{2} - 1}{R} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{2} - {\mu}_{1}}{R}$

$⇒ {f}_{eq} = \dfrac{R}{{\mu}_{2} - {\mu}_{1}}$

When joined together

$\dfrac{1}{{f}_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{{f}_{1}} + \dfrac{1}{{f}_{2}} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{2} - 1}{- R} + \dfrac{{\mu}_{2} - 1}{R} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{2} - {\mu}_{1}}{R}$

$⇒ {f}_{eq} = \dfrac{R}{{\mu}_{2} - {\mu}_{1}}$

questions.q: A point source of light, S is placed at a distance L in front of the center of plane mirror of width d which is hanging vertically on a wall. A man walks in front of the mirror along a line parallel to the mirror, at a distance 2L as shown below. The distance over which the man can see the image of the light source in the mirror is:
questions.solution:
By similar triangles

$\DeltaAEC ~ \DeltaIHA$

$\dfrac{y}{2L} = \dfrac{\dfrac{d}{2}}{L}$ (by properties of similar triangles)
$⇒ y = d$
$∴$Total distance $\left(CD\right) = y + \dfrac{d}{2} + \dfrac{d}{2} + y = 3d$

questions.q: A light wave is incident normally on a glass slab of refractive index $1.5 .$ If $4%$ of light gets reflected and the amplitude of the electric field of the incident light is $30\dfrac{V}{m},$ then the amplitude of the electric field for the wave propagating in the glass medium will be:
questions.solution:
$n =$ refractive index $= \sqrt{{ε}_{r}{\mu}_{r}}$
$I = \dfrac{1}{2}{ε}_{0}{E}_{0}^{2}C$

${I}^{′} = \dfrac{1}{2}ε{E}^{2}V$

${I}^{′} = 0.96I$

$\dfrac{1}{2}ε{E}^{2}v = 0.96\dfrac{1}{2}{ε}_{0}{E}_{0}^{2}C$

$E = \sqrt{0.96}\sqrt{\dfrac{{ε}_{0}}{{ε}_{0}{ε}_{r}}}\sqrt{\dfrac{c}{v}}{E}_{0}$

(For most of the transparent medium ${\mu}_{r} \approx 1$ )
$⇒ E = \sqrt{0.96} . \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{{ε}_{r}{\mu}_{r}}} . \sqrt{\dfrac{c}{v}}{E}_{0}$

$= \sqrt{0.96} . \dfrac{1}{n} . \sqrt{n}{E}_{0}$

$E = \sqrt{\dfrac{0.96}{n}}{E}_{0}E = \sqrt{\dfrac{0 . 96}{1 . 5}} \times 30 = 24\dfrac{V}{m}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A plano-convex lens of refractive index ${\mu}_{1}$ and focal length ${f}_{1}$ is kept in contact with another plano-concave lens of refractive index ${\mu}_{2}$ and focal length ${f}_{2} .$ If the radius of curvature of their spherical faces is $R$ each and ${f}_{1} = 2{f}_{2},$ the ${\mu}_{1}$ and ${\mu}_{2}$ are related as:
questions.solution:
Given,

${f}_{1} = 2{f}_{2}$

Lens maker formula for the first lens is given by,

$\dfrac{1}{{f}_{1}} = \left({\mu}_{1} - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{\infty}\right)\text{...(}1\text{)}$

Lens maker formula for the second lens is given by,

$\dfrac{1}{{f}_{2}} = \left({\mu}_{2} - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{\infty}\right)\text{...(}2\text{)}$

After $\dfrac{\left(1\right)}{\left(2\right)}$, we get:

$\dfrac{{f}_{2}}{{f}_{1}} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{1} - 1}{{\mu}_{2} - 1} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ 2{\mu}_{1} - 2 = {\mu}_{2} - 1$

$⇒ 2{\mu}_{1} - {\mu}_{2} = 1$

$\dfrac{1}{{f}_{1}} = \left({\mu}_{1} - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{\infty}\right)\text{...(}1\text{)}$

Lens maker formula for the second lens is given by,

$\dfrac{1}{{f}_{2}} = \left({\mu}_{2} - 1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{R} - \dfrac{1}{\infty}\right)\text{...(}2\text{)}$

After $\dfrac{\left(1\right)}{\left(2\right)}$, we get:

$\dfrac{{f}_{2}}{{f}_{1}} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{1} - 1}{{\mu}_{2} - 1} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ 2{\mu}_{1} - 2 = {\mu}_{2} - 1$

$⇒ 2{\mu}_{1} - {\mu}_{2} = 1$

questions.q: A convergent doublet of separated lenses, corrected for spherical aberration, has resultant focal length of $10 \mathrm{~cm}$. The separation between the two lenses is $2 \mathrm{~cm}$. The focal lengths of the component lenses
questions.solution:
For minimum spherical aberration separation, $d=f_1-f_2=2 \mathrm{~cm}$

questions.q: A particle is oscillating on the $\mathrm{X}$-axis with an amplitude $2 \mathrm{~cm}$ about the point $x_0=10 \mathrm{~cm}$ with a frequency $\omega$. A concave mirror of focal length 5 $\mathrm{cm}$ is placed at the origin (see figure) Identify the correct statements: (A) The image executes periodic motion (B) The image executes non-periodic motion (C) The turning points of the image are asymmetric w.r.t the image of the point at $x$=10 \mathrm{~cm}$ (D) The distance between the turning points of the oscillation of the image is $\frac{100}{21}$
questions.solution:
When object is at $8 \mathrm{~cm}$
Image $V_1=\frac{\mathrm{f} \times \mathrm{u}}{\mathrm{u}-\mathrm{f}}=\frac{5 \times 8}{8-5}=-\frac{40}{3} \mathrm{~cm}$
When object is at $12 \mathrm{~cm}$
Image $\mathrm{V}_2=\frac{\mathrm{f} \times \mathrm{u}}{\mathrm{u}-\mathrm{f}}=\frac{5 \times 12}{12-5}=-\frac{60}{7} \mathrm{~cm}$
Separation $=\left|\mathrm{V}_1-\mathrm{V}_2\right|=\frac{40}{3}-\frac{60}{7}=\frac{100}{21} \mathrm{~cm}$
So $\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{C}$ and $\mathrm{D}$ are correct statements.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Let the refractive index of a denser medium with respect to rarer medium be ${n}_{12}$ and its critical angle be ${\theta}_{C}$ . At an angle of incidence $A$ when light is travelling from denser medium to rarer medium, a part of the light is reflected and the rest is refracted and the angle between reflected and refracted rays is ${90}^{o}$. Angle $A$ is given by
questions.solution:
In accordance with Snell's law, $\mu = \dfrac{{\mu}_{R}}{{\mu}_{D}} = \dfrac{sin ⁡ {i}_{c}}{sin ⁡ {90}^{o}}$

here ${i}_{c}$ is the angle of incidence.

$\dfrac{{\mu}_{R}}{{\mu}_{D}} = sin ⁡ {i}_{c}$

$\mu = \dfrac{{\mu}_{R}}{{\mu}_{D}} = \dfrac{sin ⁡ A}{sin ⁡ r}$

$= \dfrac{sinA}{sin\left(90 ° - A\right)} = \dfrac{sinA}{cosA}$

$\dfrac{{\mu}_{R}}{{\mu}_{D}} = tan ⁡ A$.

The critical angle is related to the angle $A$ as $tan ⁡ A = sin ⁡ {\theta}_{C}$

$A = \tan^{- 1} ⁡ \left(sin ⁡ {\theta}_{C}\right)$.

questions.q: A diverging lens with magnitude of focal length $25cm$ is placed at a distance of $15cm$ from a converging lens of magnitude of focal length $20cm$. A beam of parallel light falls on the diverging lens. The final image formed is:
options: Real and at a distance of $6cm$ from the convergent lens
Real and at a distance of $40cm$ from convergent lens
Virtual and at a distance of $40cm$ from convergent lens
Real and at a distance of $40cm$ from the divergent lens
questions.solution:
Diverging lens forms the image at its focus. The image formed by diverging lens is the object for converging lens.

$∴$ Distance of the object from converging lens is $40cm$ i.e., object is at double focal point.

$∴$ Image forms at double focal point on the other side of the lens.
$\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{1}{f}$
$\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{\left(- 40\right)} = \dfrac{1}{20}$
$\dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{40} = \dfrac{1}{20}$
$\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{20} - \dfrac{1}{40} = \dfrac{1}{40}$
$v = 40$

questions.q: A thin convex lens of focal length $f$ is put on a plane mirror as shown in the figure. When an object is kept at a distance $a$ from the lens-mirror combination, its image is formed at a distance $\dfrac{a}{3}$ in front of the combination. The value of $a$ is:
questions.solution:
Equivalent power of combination is

${P}_{eff} = 2{P}_{lens} + {P}_{mirror}$ ...(i)

$∵ {P}_{mirror} = 0$ for plane mirror and ${P}_{lens} = \dfrac{1}{f}$

Also combination behaves as a mirror. So. ${P}_{eff} = \dfrac{1}{{f}_{mirror}}$

In equation (i)

$- \dfrac{1}{{f}_{mirror}} = \dfrac{2}{f} ⇒ {f}_{mirror} = - \dfrac{f}{2}$

By mirror formula

$\dfrac{1}{{f}_{mirror}} = \dfrac{1}{u} + \dfrac{1}{v}$

Here $u = - a, v = - \dfrac{a}{3}, {f}_{mirror} = - \dfrac{f}{2}$

$⇒ - \dfrac{2}{f} = \dfrac{1}{- a} + \dfrac{3}{- a} = \dfrac{- 4}{a}$

$⇒ \dfrac{- 2}{f} = \dfrac{- 4}{a} ⇒ a = 2f$

questions.q: Monochromatic light is incident on a glass prism of angle A. If the refractive index of the material of the prism is $\mu$ , a ray, incident at an angle $\theta$ , on the face AB would get transmitted through the face AC of the prism provided:
questions.solution:
Central Idea: The ray will get transmitted through face $AC$ if ${i}_{AC} < {i}_{C}$

Consider the ray diagram is shown below.

A ray of light incident on face $AB$ at an angle $\theta$

${r}_{1} =$ Angle of refraction on face $AB$

${r}_{2} =$ Angle of incidence at face $AC$

For transmission of light through face $AC$

${i}_{AC} < {i}_{C}$

or $A - {r}_{1} < {i}_{C}$

or $sin\left(A - {r}_{1}\right) < sin{i}_{C}$

or $sin\left(A - {r}_{1}\right) < \dfrac{1}{\mu}$

$A - {r}_{1} < \sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\mu}\right)$

or $sin{r}_{1} > sin\left[A - \sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\mu}\right)\right]$

Now, applying Snell's law at the face $AB$

$1 \times sin\theta = \musin{r}_{1}$

or $sin{r}_{1} = \dfrac{sin\theta}{\mu}$

$⇒ \dfrac{sin\theta}{\mu} > sin\left[A - \sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\mu}\right)\right]$

or $\theta > \sin^{- 1}\left[\musin\left\{A - \sin^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\mu}\right)\right\}\right]$

The relative refractive index of the two media is
questions.solution:
${\mu}_{1}:$ refractive index of rarer medium

${\mu}_{2}:$ retractive index of denser medium

${sin \theta}_{C} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{1}}{{\mu}_{2}}$

${tan \theta}_{B} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{1}}{{\mu}_{2}}$

$sin{\theta}_{C} = tan{\theta}_{B}$

$tan{\theta}_{B} = \dfrac{{\mu}_{1}}{{\mu}_{2}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{1 - {( \dfrac{1}{1.28} )}^{2}}}{( \dfrac{1}{1.28} )}$

$= 0.8$

questions.q: The refractive index of the material of a concave lens is $\mu$. It is immersed in a medium of refractive index $\mu_1$. A parallel beam of light is incident on the lens. The path of the emergent rays when $\mu_1>\mu$ is:
questions.question: The refractive index of the material of a concave lens is $\mu$. It is immersed in a medium of refractive index $\mu_1$. A parallel beam of light is incident on the lens. The path of the emergent rays when $\mu_1>\mu$ is:
questions.explanation:
If a lens of refractive index $\mu$ is immersed in a medium of refractive index $\mu_1$, then its focal length in medium is given by
$
\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{m}}}=\left({ }_{\mathrm{m}} \mu_l-1\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}_1}\right)-\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}_2}\right)
$
If $\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{a}}$ is the focal length of lens in air, then
$
\begin{aligned}
&\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{a}}}=\left({ }_{\mathrm{a}} \mu_l-1\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}_1}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}_2}\right)\right. \\
&\Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{m}}}{\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{a}}}=\frac{\left({ }_{\mathrm{a}} \mu_l-1\right)}{\left({ }_{\mathrm{m}} \mu_l-1\right)}
\end{aligned}
$
If $\mu_1>\mu$, then $\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{m}}$ and $\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{a}}$ have opposite signs and the nature of lens changes i.e. a convex lens diverges the light rays and concave lens converges the light rays. Thus given option (a) is correct.

questions.q: An object is located in a fixed position in front of a screen. Sharp image is obtained on the screen for two positions of a thin lens separated by 10 $\mathrm{cm}$. The size of the images in two situations are in the ratio $3: 3$. What is the distance between the screen and the object?
questions.solution:
Given: Separation of lens for two of its position, $d=10 \mathrm{~cm}$ Ratio of size of the images in two positions

$\frac{I_1}{I_2}=\frac{3}{2}$Distance of object from the screen, $D=$ ? Applying formula,

$\begin{aligned}$&$\frac{I_1}{I_2}=\frac{(D+d)^2}{(D-d)^2}$\\
&\Rightarrow \quad $\frac{3}{2}=\frac{(D+10)^2}{(D-10)^2}$\\
&\Rightarrow \quad $\frac{3}{2}=\frac{D^2+100+20 D}{D^2+100-20 D}$\\
&\Rightarrow 3 D²+300-60 D=2 D²+200+40 D \\
&\Rightarrow D²-100 D+100=0
\end{aligned}

On solving, we get $D=99 \mathrm{~cm}$
Hence the distance between the screen and the object is $99 \mathrm{~cm}$.

questions.q: The focal length of the objective and the eyepiece of a telescope are $50 \mathrm{~cm}$ and $5 \mathrm{~cm}$ respectively. If the telescope is focussed for distinct vision on a scale distant $2 \mathrm{~m}$ from its objective, then its magnifying power will be :
questions.solution:
Given: $\mathrm{f}_0=50 \mathrm{ cm}, \mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{e}}=5 \mathrm{ cm}\mathrm{d}=25 \mathrm{ cm}, \mathrm{u}_0=-200 \mathrm{ cm}$
Magnification $\mathrm{M}=$ ?
As $\frac{1}{\mathrm{v}_0}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{u}_0}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}_0} ⇒ \frac{1}{\mathrm{v}_0}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}_0}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{u}_0}=\frac{1}{50}-\frac{1}{200}=\frac{4-1}{200}=\frac{3}{200}$ or $\mathrm{v}_0=\frac{200}{3} \mathrm{ cm}$
Now $\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{e}}=\mathrm{d}=-25 \mathrm{ cm}$
From, $\frac{1}{v_e}-\frac{1}{u_e}=\frac{1}{f_e} \begin{aligned}& -\frac{1}{u_e}=\frac{1}{f_e}-\frac{1}{v_e}\\
& =\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1}{25}=\frac{6}{25}
\end{aligned}$ or, $\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{e}}=\frac{-25}{6} \mathrm{ cm} \begin{aligned}& \text{ Magnification } \mathrm{M}=\mathrm{M} }_{0} \times \mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{e}}\\
  =\frac{\mathrm{v}_0}{\mathrm{u}_0} \times \frac{\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{e}}}{\mathrm{u}_{\mathrm{e}}}=\frac{-200 / 3}{200} \times \frac{-25}{-25 / 6}\\
 =-\frac{1}{3} \times6=-2
\end{aligned}
$

suffer total internal reflection in case (B) only

have partial reflection and partial transmission in case (B)

have $100 \%$ transmission in case (A)

Velocity of light in medium

$\mathrm{V}_{\text{med }}=\frac{3 \mathrm{ cm}}{0.2 \mathrm{ ns}}=\frac{3 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{ m}}{0.2 \times 10^{-9} \mathrm{ s}}=$1.5 $\mathrm{ m}$/ $\mathrm{s}Refractive index of $the medium

\mu=$\frac{V_{\text{air }}}{V_{\text{med }}}=\frac{3 \times 10^8}{1.5}=$2 $\mathrm{ m}$/ $\mathrm{s}$ As $\mu=\frac{1}{\sin C}$
\therefore \sin $\mathrm{C}=\frac{1}{\mu}=\frac{1}{2}=$30^{{}^{\circ}}

Condition of $TIR is angle of incidence i must be greater than critical angle. Hence ray will suffer TIR in case of(B)   \left(i=40^{{}^{\circ}} \gt 30^{{}^{\circ}}\right) only.$

questions.q: We wish to make a microscope with the help of two positive lenses both with a focal length of 20 $\mathrm{mm}$ each and the object is positioned $25 \mathrm{~mm}$ from the objective lens. How far apart the lenses should be so that the final image is formed at infinity?
questions.solution: To obtain final image at infinity, object which is the image formed by objective should be at focal distance of eye-piece. By lens formula (for objective) $\begin{aligned}$& $\frac{1}{v_0}-\frac{1}{u_0}=\frac{1}{f_0}$\\ $\text{ or, } \quad$& $\frac{1}{v_0}-\frac{1}{-25}=\frac{1}{20}$\\ \Rightarrow \quad & $\frac{1}{v_0}=\frac{1}{20}-\frac{1}{25}=\frac{5-4}{100}=\frac{1}{100} \mathrm{~mm}$\\ \therefore \quad & v_0=100 $\mathrm{~mm} \end{aligned}$Therefore the distance between the lenses =v_0+f_e=100 $\mathrm{~mm}+$20 $\mathrm{~mm}=$120 $\mathrm{~mm}$

An initially parallel cylindrical beam travels in a medium of refractive index $\mu(I)=\mu_0+\mu_2 I$, where $\mu_0$ and $\mu_2$ are positive constants and $\mathrm{I}$ is the intensity of the light beam. The intensity of the beam is decreasing with increasing radius.
The initial shape of the wave front of the beam is
options:
convex

concave

convex near the axis and concave near the periphery

planar
questions.solution: For a parallel cylindrical beam, wavefront will be planar.

questions.q: A plane convex lens of refractive index $1.5$ and radius of curvature $30 \mathrm{~cm}$ is silvered at the curved surface. Now this lens has been used to form the image of an object. At what distance from this lens an object be placed in order to have a real image of the size of the object?
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}$& $\frac{1}{F}=\frac{2}{f_1}+\frac{1}{f_m}$\\
& $\text{$ and $} \frac{1}{f_1}=($1.5-1)$\left(\frac{1}{\infty}-\frac{1}{-30}\right)=\frac{1}{60}$\\
& $\text{$ and }f_m=15 $\mathrm{~cm} .$\\
& \therefore F=10 $\mathrm{~cm} .
\end{aligned}$Object should be placed at $20 \mathrm{~cm}$ from the lens.
